Pembrolizumab is not given in every arm (there is a DCSZ11 monotherapy arm), is not GBM standard of care, and its combination with DCSZ11 is the tested regimen ("determine DCSZ11 Phase 1b doses in combination with pembrolizumab"), so rule 3 does not apply. Against that, it is a fixed approved partner whose own dose is not studied, which could be read as backbone. No ruling covers this. D31-B13 settles this: an approved drug fixed in some arms whose dose is not studied is a candidate (experimental_combination).

As above. In GBM patients (Phase 1a Part 2 only) pembrolizumab is not background therapy, so it counts as a second investigational agent. This makes the trial contain an approved-drug candidate (origin category 2), which is why XL should confirm. D31-B13 settles this: an approved drug fixed in some arms whose dose is not studied is a candidate (experimental_combination).

GBM patients can enter only Phase 1a (DCSZ11 alone, or DCSZ11 + pembrolizumab). D31-C2 lists co-candidates, and in baskets the GBM arms are coded (D31-C3), so doxorubicin and tebentafusp (non-GBM SOC cohorts) are not partners.

note: Pembrolizumab is a candidate under D31-B13, so the trial's origin group includes an approved drug (repurposing_containing). Still open: DCSZ11's role differs by GBM arm (experimental_monotherapy in Phase 1a Part 1, experimental_combination in Part 2); no ruling or convention picks one, and either keeps it a candidate (low confidence). any_molecular_selection is now false under D31-A1 (MSS-CRC and the NSCLC driver-mutation exclusions apply only to non-GBM Phase 1b cohorts). Regimen stays combination (GBM arms mixed, D31-C3). GBM is named in inclusion notes, so it is a basket under D27B.
